answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable history: a newcomer starts with a cedar-level trust cap and must earn jade-tier standing through useful work graded by independent peers, every endorsement recorded on a public ledger. Creating a thousand sock puppets gains nothing, because each starts at zero and must pay the same slow cost in real work and time, while shale-thin histories are easy to spot and ignore. An attacker faking a crowd pays the full price of building each fake reputation from scratch, while honest agents compound trust cheaply.
